blocks.text: Standard electrode potentials are used to deduce the direction of electron flow in a cell (10.17.1), to predict whether a redox reaction is feasible (10.17.2), and to compare the strengths of oxidising and reducing agents (10.17.3). The next three topics treat each application.

blocks.prompt: Name the three uses of E standard values treated in this chapter.
blocks.explanation: Finding the direction of electron flow in the external circuit, judging whether a proposed redox reaction is feasible from the sign of E cell, and ranking species as oxidising or reducing agents by how positive or negative their E standard values are.

items: Applications of E standard: direction of electron flow; feasibility of a reaction; relative strength of oxidising and reducing agents.
